header.attestation.dateTime.description: Date and time of the approval of the document by the attester.

header.language.description: Language in which the document is written. Language is expressed by the IETF language tag.

header.documentCategory.description: Broad category of document (e.g. 34105-7 Hospital discharge summary).

header.documentType.description: Type of document (e.g. 34106-5 Physician hospital discharge summary).

header.documentTitle.description: Human-readable document title that may be displayed in search results etc. This may be documentType’s display name or it may contain further information. Example: ‘Hospital discharge report. Jane Green. 7.10.2025-10.10.2025’.

header.period.description: Time period of information covered in the document.

header.legalAuthentication.legalAuthenti.description: The person or organisation taking responsibility for the content of the document.

header.legalAuthentication.dateTime.description: Date and time when the document was authenticated.

header.eventCategory.description: Categorisation of the event covered by the document (e.g. discharge type). Selection of such tags or labels depends on the use case and agreement between data-sharing parties. This metadata element serves primarily for searching and filtering purposes.

header.serviceSpecialty.description: Additional details about where the content was created (e.g. clinical speciality).

header.custodian.description: Organisation that is in charge of maintaining the document.

header.countryOfOrigin.description: Country of origin of the document.

header.intendedRecipient[x].description: Intended recipient of the information, i.e. a person or organisation that shall be notified or be aware of the content. This element is used to indicate explicit communication intent and does not represent routine storage or passive availability of information (e.g. in portals).

presentedForm.description: A narrative easy-to-read representation of the full dataset, e.g. PDF version of a document. At least one of body or presentedForm shall be present.

body.description: Discharge report structured body. At least one of body or presentedForm shall be present.

body.alerts.generatedNarrative.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section.

body.alerts.medicalAlert.description: Medical alerts relevant in the context of the encounter.

body.encounterInformation.generatedNarra.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section.

body.encounterInformation.note.description: Free text notes by the health professional.

body.admissionEvaluation.description: Section: Admission evaluation. Admission evaluation section shall be reported only if it is relevant to ensure continuity of care.

body.admissionEvaluation.generatedNarrat.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section.

body.admissionEvaluation.objectiveFindin.description: Objective findings, such as anthropometric measurements, vital signs or objective anatomical findings of physical examination.

body.admissionEvaluation.functionalStatu.description: An individual’s ability to perform normal daily activities required to meet basic needs, fulfil usual roles and maintain health and well-being.

body.admissionEvaluation.note.description: Free text notes by the evaluation performer.

body.patientHistory.description: Section: Patient health history (anamnesis) containing only information that is highly relevant to this specific episode of care. The model is designed with the expectation that the patient summary is available.

body.patientHistory.generatedNarrative.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section. If the section includes structured information, it shall also be included in generatedNarrative.

body.patientHistory.pastProblems[x].description: A list of conditions that a patient suffered from in the past or still suffers from. Unlike the diagnostic summary, the medical history is not only a list of problems but may also contain a broader description of the condition and its progress, details about treatment, including medication and patient response to treatment. The past problem section (unlike the same section of the patient summary) shall include only conditions that are important for continuity of care. This section, if provided, complements the diagnostic summary section of the discharge report.

body.patientHistory.devicesAndImplants.description: Devices and implants in patient anamnesis.

body.patientHistory.note.description: Free text notes by the health professional.

body.courseOfEncounter.description: Section: Course of inpatient or outpatient encounter.

body.courseOfEncounter.generatedNarrativ.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section.

body.courseOfEncounter.conditionSummary.description: Conditions that were treated or affected provisioning of care (diagnostics, therapy, nursing, monitoring) during the encounter. At least one attended condition shall be marked. Other conditions are recorded only if they are important for continuity of care (after discharge).

body.courseOfEncounter.procedures.description: Procedures performed during encounter which are significant for continuity of care, e.g. surgeries and other instrumental interventions (endoscopic, intravascular), chemotherapy, radiotherapy, purification methods (dialysis, haemoperfusion), circulation support methods (counterpulsation etc.), administration of blood derivatives or others. Diagnostic procedures are typically captured as observation results and not repeated here.

body.courseOfEncounter.medicalDevicesAnd.description: Medical devices (including implants) whose use was started, stopped or otherwise modified during the encounter.

body.courseOfEncounter.objectiveFindings.description: Objective findings, such as anthropometric measurements, vital signs or objective anatomical findings of physical examination. The line between objective findings and test results is not clear and it is up to the implementers to decide how to logically display different measurements.

body.courseOfEncounter.testResults[x].description: Significant medical test results of functional, diagnostic (including laboratory) and imaging examinations performed during encounter.

body.courseOfEncounter.note.description: Free text notes by the health professional.

body.dischargeDetails.generatedNarrative.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section.

body.dischargeDetails.objectiveFindings.description: Objective findings, such as anthropometric measurements, vital signs or objective anatomical findings of physical examination.

body.dischargeDetails.functionalStatus[x.description: An individual’s ability to perform normal daily activities required to meet basic needs, fulfil usual roles and maintain health and well-being.

body.dischargeDetails.note.description: Free text notes by the health professional.

body.medicationSummary.description: Summary information on the medication recommended for the period after discharge, indicating whether the medication is changed or newly started. Compared to previous practices, the overview is supplemented with medication that has been discontinued.

body.medicationSummary.generatedNarrativ.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section.

body.medicationSummary.note.description: Free text notes by the health professional.

body.carePlan.description: Section: Care plan and other recommendations after discharge.

body.carePlan.generatedNarrative.description: Narrative, potentially formatted, content of the whole section.

body.carePlan.otherRecommendations.description: Other recommendations (advice) after discharge, e.g. recommendation to suggest hip replacement, reduce number of cigarettes, stop smoking, increase physical exercise.

use.description: Purpose of the address. If this attribute is not present, the address is assumed to be the default address useful for any purpose.

type.description: Distinguishes between physical addresses (those that may be visited) and mailing addresses. Most addresses are both.

dosageDetails.note.description: Patient-oriented instructions as free text for this dosage step.

dosageDetails.doseAndRate.description: Amount of medication administered per dose (= one timing).

dosageDetails.doseAndRate.rate[x].description: Amount of medication per time period (e.g. 100 mg per hour). When rate is provided per time unit, Quantity data type may be used with a suitable unit (e.g. mg/h, μg/min.).
